column1: # Source surface → the rule an edit there has to keep. One source of truth, read by the
# contentworker-conventions skill, the review-change skill and .claude/hooks/rules-impact.sh,
# which says the matching rules once per file per session. Columns are TAB-separated:
#   2. the reminder: what the rule is and what to do, in one or two sentences
# Every row that matches a path is said, so keep rows narrow and reminders short. The reasoning
# behind each rule is in invariants.md. .claude/scripts/toolkit-check.sh fails when a regex

column2: The domain depends on nothing: no @contentworker/* package, no framework, no I/O, no platform binding type. Pure functions over domain types; tests in packages/domain/test.

Content is structured, not serialized HTML: rich text is a RichTextDocument tree end to end. HTML comes in only through richTextFromHtml and goes out only in the consumer's renderer; never store, return or emit content as markup.

Ports are interfaces only, in domain types: no SQL, Drizzle, database binding or HTTP type crosses a port. A new ContentStore method needs the in-memory store in packages/test-kit and the SQL store in packages/db, with a contract test in packages/db/test.

Use-cases take AppContext and a Scope, get ids from ctx.ids.newId() and time from ctx.clock.now(), and never import an adapter. A new capability is exposed through BOTH a route in packages/http/src/api/routes/management/<area>.ts and a tool in packages/http/src/mcp/tools/<area>.ts (new-use-case skill), with a test in packages/application/test on @contentworker/test-kit fakes.

withTransaction is a unit of work, not an interactive transaction: read everything first, then write; a read inside the unit doesn't see its own writes; a compare-and-set loses as TransactionConflictError at commit (retry or treat as a no-op). The outbox event rides in the same unit.
The relay and the queue consumers run at least once: every handler is idempotent on the event id (a redelivered event must not double-send a webhook or double-embed).

The in-memory store must behave like the SQL store: unit-of-work semantics (reads don't see the unit's own writes, conflicts surface at commit as TransactionConflictError). A fake laxer than the database hides bugs.

The database binds at most 100 parameters per statement: use chunked / selectChunked or one JSON parameter with json_each for any list. One writer per database: no writes on read paths (throttle things like lastUsedAt). Contract tests in packages/db/test run in the local runtime against a local database.

Hand-written SQL, expand-only, never edited once on origin/main (the guard-invariants hook denies it). Mirror every change in packages/db/src/schema.ts (or auth-schema.ts) and apply locally with `pnpm --filter @contentworker/web db:migrate:local` (d1-migration skill).
schema.ts mirrors the SQL migrations column for column; changing it alone changes no database. Write the next numbered migration in packages/db/migrations in the same change (d1-migration skill).

An adapter implements one port and is bound only in packages/platform/src/wire.ts or an app entry, chosen from env. It runs on the edge-worker runtime: fetch and bindings, no filesystem, no long-lived sockets. Keep binding and SDK types inside the adapter; tests in packages/adapters/test/<name>.

Composition root and env surface: a new var or binding goes in EdgeEnv (env.ts), config.ts, every apps/*/wrangler.jsonc that reads it, scripts/fleet.ts if it varies per deployment, and docs/configuration.md. Secrets are never vars: CI writes them (fleet.ts SECRETS).

A new stateful-object class is exported by apps/engine, gets a migration tag appended in apps/engine/wrangler.jsonc and in scripts/do-migrations.test.ts in the same change, and api/delivery bind it by script_name. Never rename or delete a class that holds data.
Durable-workflow code replays: side effects, clock reads and model calls only inside step.do, and step names never change once deployed (a renamed step loses its cached result for running instances).
Agent workflow functions are deterministic: every side effect goes through the Activities interface, so the same code runs in-process and under durable workflows.

Routes are thin: authorize against the route's space, parse with the zod schema the OpenAPI doc uses, call the use-case, serialize. The same capability must exist as an MCP tool in packages/http/src/mcp/tools/<area>.ts. A management route goes in its area's file under routes/management/ (a new area adds its own file and one line in management.ts's AREAS), with its response schema in api/docs/schemas/<area>.ts imported from that file, never a barrel. No trailing-z paths.

MCP tools call the same application use-cases as the HTTP routes with the same authorization, so an agent can never do what an API client can't, or the reverse. A tool goes in its area's file, packages/http/src/mcp/tools/<area>.ts (a new area adds its own file and one line in server.ts's TOOL_AREAS). A tool that changes nothing declares `annotations: { readOnlyHint: true }` (or READ_ONLY) so the audit trail skips it; anything else is audited.
The MCP skills are embedded into packages/http/src/mcp/skills.generated.ts: it is gitignored and rebuilt by `pnpm install` and every turbo check-types, test and build; never commit it.

This is the template scripts/fleet.ts renders per deployment: a new resource name or id needs fleet.ts, scripts/provision.sh, and provisioning in every deployment before the merge that binds it. Stateful-object migration tags are append-only (infra-change skill); `pnpm test:fleet` checks it.
The fleet registry and its renderer: run `pnpm test:fleet`. A deployment missing a resource stops CI's plan; rollout order is in the infra-change skill.
APPLIED is frozen: only append the same entry a new class appends to apps/engine/wrangler.jsonc. DESTRUCTIVE_ALLOWED stays empty unless the class's data has been planned with the user.

Trust-boundary code: x-cw-principal is believed only when signed with PRINCIPAL_KEY, bound to the path and under 60 s old; the Delivery entrypoint is never routable; keys are stored hashed; outbound URLs pass url-safety. Have the security-reviewer agent look at this change before you finish.

The admin: read PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md ("Ledger") and compose packages/ui and the existing components, never stock shadcn defaults. Logic tests in apps/web/tests (*.test.ts node, *.test.tsx jsdom); routes and flows in apps/web/e2e (testing skill).
Public SDKs depend only on @contentworker/sdk-* packages, never on server code, and run on fetch alone. Their exports are a public API: changes are additive or called out as breaking.

docs/*.md is embedded into packages/docs/src/generated.ts: it is gitignored and rebuilt by `pnpm install` and every turbo check-types, test and build; never commit it. Never name a competing CMS; say "the surveyed CMS".

Actions pinned by full SHA, `permissions: contents: read` unless a job needs more, verify steps keep `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`, no untrusted ${{ github.event.* }} in run:, deploy order engine → api → delivery → web and rollback engine first.
Toolkit change: run `pnpm test:toolkit`, and update .claude/README.md when you add or change an agent, skill or hook. Hook wiring lives in settings.json and takes effect in a new session.
